event.name: June 2020 Saharan dust outbreak to Caribbean and U.S.

formulas.scenario: increase winds by 15 percent, temperature by 2 C, and exposure counts by 25 percent; recompute transport, exposure, and index

judge_anchors: Event window is 2020-06-14 through 2020-06-28, 15 days inclusive.
Event scene is 7 days after the window start; pre-scene gap is 30 days.
Brightness delta is -2.888 and red-blue delta is 1.358, giving plume_visibility_norm 0.534.
Point dry fraction is 0.800 and regional precipitation mean is 30.1 mm, giving dry_scavenging_resistance 0.694.
Exposure counts are 973 roads, 27 critical amenities, and 12 access-sensitive features.
Baseline index is 57.2; warmer/windier exposure-growth scenario index is 60.8 with delta 3.6.

primary_gt.final_interpretation: The sampled sector shows a moderate dust-operational stress signal: transient haze/color change is supported by dry persistence and nontrivial exposure, while the scenario raises the index mainly through stronger mixing and higher exposed-load assumptions.

mechanism_chain: official event context identifies a June 2020 Saharan dust outbreak reaching the Caribbean and United States
paired true-color scenes show event-window haze/color change over the sampled sector
low annual embedding change reduces the chance that the signal is persistent land-surface change
mostly dry point records and moderate regional precipitation imply incomplete local rain scavenging
wind, warm daily maxima, exposed population, roads, and critical amenities set the operational response load

response_priorities.basis: plume visibility, dry scavenging resistance, and exposed population make health messaging and visibility caution the leading action.
the AOI contains many road elements and access-sensitive features that could be affected by haze-related visibility degradation.
hospitals, schools, police, fire, and shelter amenities are present in the sampled sector and should be prepared for air-quality inquiries.

criteria.name: Event timing and image-signal extraction

criteria.description: Correctly computes surface-confound resistance, point dry-day fractions, regional precipitation mean, dry-scavenging resistance, wind conversion, ERA5 vector wind, and transport-mixing normalization.
criteria.name: Atmospheric persistence and confound handling

criteria.description: Correctly estimates AOI area, population density, road elements, critical amenities, access-sensitive features, and exposure-pressure normalization.

criteria.description: Applies the weighted baseline index and warmer, windier, 25 percent exposure-growth scenario with correct scenario delta.
criteria.name: Baseline and scenario calculations

criteria.description: Explains the chain from trans-Atlantic dust/haze expression through low local rainout, transport support, and sampled operational exposure without claiming the AOI is the full plume footprint.
criteria.name: Disaster-process interpretation
